headline: Last session: Sensex slipped into red while Nifty gained 75 points; smallcaps showed resilience amid mixed global cues.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Profit booking in large-cap stocks led the Sensex to slip into the red.
Concerns over a three-day banking strike starting Monday weighed on financial sector sentiment.
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Houthi attacks impacted global risk appetite.
Warnings of cyberattacks on the emerging semiconductor ecosystem created cautiousness in tech.
whatHappening: Nifty 50 managed to close with a 75-point gain despite volatility in the Sensex.
Small-cap stocks outperformed the benchmarks in the previous trading session.
Market participants are closely monitoring crude oil prices and FII activity for next week's direction.
The Finance Ministry is coordinating with bank chiefs to ensure services during the upcoming strike.

summary: The Indian market ended the last session on a mixed note as the Nifty gained 75 points while the Sensex faced selling pressure. Geopolitical tensions and an impending three-day banking strike have kept investors on edge over the weekend. Markets remain closed today and will reopen on Monday with a focus on FII flows and crude oil trends.
